candidates.tagline: 12 years to ship GTA VI. PSN went down. You still couldn't play it.
candidates.story: GTA VI launched November 19, 2026 — 12 years after GTA V — but Sony's PlayStation Network went down twice: first the afternoon before launch, then again at the US midnight unlock; players who had already downloaded the game found themselves locked out of single-player mode because Sony requires internet authentication even to start a solo game.
candidates.why_funny: The game that took 12 years to ship requires the internet to play offline — and on the one night every gamer was watching, that internet connection wasn't there.
candidates.alt: The Sony Interactive Entertainment headquarters building in San Mateo, California, lit with event lighting at night — the company that runs PlayStation Network, which suffered two outages on the night GTA VI finally launched

candidates.tagline: Outlook died for a day across 70 countries. Microsoft's response: more AI.
candidates.story: On November 12–13, 2026, a nearly 24-hour Microsoft 365 outage disrupted Outlook, Exchange, Teams, and Copilot across more than 70 countries, with 80% of servers unresponsive at the peak; five days later, Satya Nadella opened Microsoft Ignite 2026 by addressing the outage, called digital infrastructure 'the dial tone for the world,' then announced Copilot as 'the new OS for work' and asked enterprises to trust Microsoft AI with their entire business workflow.
candidates.why_funny: The pitch for 'bet your business on Microsoft AI' was delivered five days after the email platform businesses already depend on collapsed globally for a full day — with no explanation of what specifically broke.
candidates.alt: Microsoft Building 92, the visitor center at Microsoft Corporation's headquarters campus in Redmond, Washington — the company whose Microsoft 365 cloud services, including Outlook and Copilot, went offline for nearly 24 hours across 70 countries on November 12–13, 2026
